title: Stop-price rounding direction: broker stops round to the cent away from price (long DOWN, short UP) and take-profit limits toward the entry (long DOWN, short UP), instead of round(x, 2)

rules.stops: stop_px(stop, long): floor to the cent for a long stop, ceil for a short stop - never tighter than the modelled stop; used for bracket/OTO stop legs (submit_bracket), scale-out protection (OCO stop leg and plain stop, _submit_protection) and runner stop moves (breakeven / trail: move_stop, move_lot_stop)
rules.targets: target_px(target, long): floor for a long target, ceil for a short target. The backtest (mcf/backtest/engine.py) fills a target at exactly sig.target on a touch with no slippage, so the live limit rounds toward the entry to fill whenever the model's touch happens (cost < 1 cent/share); rounding away from entry could leave modelled target fills unfilled
rules.unchanged: after-hours marketable flatten limits (0.5% through the price) keep round(x, 2); scale-out breakeven be = round(fill, 2) is then floored/ceiled by stop_px (on-the-cent values unchanged); prices stay at 2 decimals
rules.tolerance: values within 1e-6 cent of a whole cent (float noise) are kept as they are

evidence: research/rootcause_1119/FINDINGS.md (ETHA 11-19: round(39.5366, 2) = 39.54, the low was exactly 39.540; about -0.9R; 1 of 89 live stops)

plain: Stop prices sent to the broker are now rounded so a stop is never closer to the price than the setup intended; profit targets are rounded so they fill whenever the backtest would have filled them.

Effect is mechanical: stops trigger at or beyond the modelled level, targets fill at or before it.
